Piṅgala
or Piṅgalanāga or Piṅgalācārya; traditionally identified with Patañjali ref. to a. younger brother of Pāṇini. by Ṣaḍguruśiṣya.
--Chandaḥśāstra or sūtra or Piṅgalachandaḥśāstra.
Pt.. (1) Bib. Ind. 74. Calcutta, 1874. (2) K. M. 91. 1908. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p.. 1917-18.
--Prākṛtapiṅgala (ascribed) but supposed to be a later compilation.
Pt.. (1) with C. of Lakṣmīnātha Bhaṭṭa. K. M. 41. 1894. (2) with C.s of Viśvanātha Pañcānana, Vam3sīdhara, Kṛṣṇa an. Yādavendra. Bib. Ind. 148. 1902.

Piṅgala

Piṅgala(ācārya)

Given a. a sup. to Vṛttaratnākara of Kedāra Bhaṭṭa in Br. Mus. 460. See NCC. III. p. 266a; also Adyar D. V. 1632. Pt.. with C. Colombo, 1888.

Piṅgalākṣa
alias Piṅgalanetra or Nīlanetra or Vimalākṣa. Bud. Mādhyamika. lived an. worked in Central Asia.
See Richard A. Gard, J. of Ind. an. Bud. Studies Tokyo II (1953-54) 1-10. [Page083-a.
--Dvādaśanikāyaśāstra. hypothetical Skt. (or Kuchean) compilation from Madhyamakārikā of Nāgārjuna.
--C. on the same known only from its Chinese transl. by Kumārajīva.
See NCC. IX. p. 192b an. Richard A. Gard. op. cit. an. J. of Ind. an. Bud. Studies III. (1954-55) English Section 7-13.

Piṅgalācārya

Piṅgalāmata
śaiva. Upāgama in Prodgītāgama.
See list in Kāmika.

Piṅgalāmata
tantra. in 19 prakaraṇas; from Jayadrathādhikāra of Brahmayāmalatantra.
Br. Mus. 550. Nepal II. p.. 69-70 (ms. d. 1174 A. D.). Rep. Hpr. 1906-11, p. 3.
Q. by Hemādri; by Raghunandana in Malamāsatattva, Oxf. 292a; Q. on Kuṇḍa-construction in Madanaratnapradīpa ms.; by Viṭṭhala Dīkṣita in his Maṇḍapakuṇḍasiddhi an. C. BBRAS. 426, Oxf. 341a; by Kṛṣṇānanda in Tantrasāra, Lz. 1272; by Rāmacandra Vājapeyin in Kuṇḍanirmāṇa, IO. 3154; by a pupil of Pragalbhācārya in vidyārṇava, RASB. VIII. A. 6206.

Piṅgalāmatasaṅgraha
or Recirājīya. jy. on prognostication (made by observing the sound, the movement etc. of certain birds). [Page083-b]
